title: Interchanging proper direct image and extension by zero
statement:
Work in the standing scheme setting of [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and let $\Lambda$ be admissible in the sense of [sk-def-localizing-closure]. For $\Lambda=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], as fixed by the chapter. Let $p:\overline X\to Y$ be proper, let
$i:Y\to\overline Y$ be a quasi-compact open immersion, and let
$\overline X\xrightarrow{j'}W\xrightarrow{r}\overline Y$ be a compactification of
$i\circ p$ in the sense of [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], with $\overline X$ dense in $W$. Then:

1. $r^{-1}(Y)=\overline X$ (as open subschemes of $W$), and $r$ restricts to $p$
over $Y$;
2. for $A\in D(\overline X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ there is a unique map
$\iota_A:i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ in $D(\overline Y_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ whose
restriction to $Y$ is the identity of $Rp_*A$;
3. $\iota_A$ is an isomorphism for every $A\in\Loc(\Dctf(\overline X,\Lambda))$.

proof.text: Put $V=r^{-1}(Y)$. The map $j'$ factors through $V$ since $rj'=ip$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $V\to Y$ is proper, hence separated by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $\overline X\to V$ proper, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] makes its image closed. This image is also open and dense in $V$ by density in $W$. Hence it is all of $V$: the open immersion identifies $\overline X$ with $V$ as schemes, and $r$ restricts to $p$.

source.place: Proof (1): the proper closed dense image argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-derived-open-square-restriction] to this Cartesian square. Write $\eta_i,\eta_{j'}$ for its invertible open units and $\lambda_A=(Rp_*\eta_{j',A})^{-1}\rho_{j'_!A}:i^*Rr_*j'_!A\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*A$. These comparisons and adjunctions are natural and compatible with shifts on the unbounded categories.

source.place: Proof (2): unbounded open restriction and its normalization.

proof.text: The open adjunction followed by $\lambda_A$ bijects maps $i_!Rp_*A\to Rr_*j'_!A$ with endomorphisms of $Rp_*A$ by $m\mapsto\lambda_A i^*(m)\eta_{i,Rp_*A}$. Define $\iota_A$ as the inverse image of the identity; bijectivity proves its uniqueness. For $f:A\to A'$, the two composites $G(f)\iota_A$ and $\iota_{A'}F(f)$, where $F=i_!Rp_*$ and $G=Rr_*j'_!$, have transpose $Rp_*f$ by naturality of $\lambda$ and $\eta_i$, so agree. The same bijection and the shift compatibility in step 2 identify $\iota_{A[n]}$ with $\iota_A[n]$.

source.place: Proof (2): elementary identity transpose, naturality and shifts.

proof.text: Let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be the closed complement. For $A\in\Dctf$, [lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero] gives $c^*G(A)=0$. Clause (4) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives $c^*i_!=0$, because its pulled-back open is empty; every sheaf on the empty scheme is zero. Thus $c^*\iota_A$ is an isomorphism; $i^*\iota_A$ is one by its normalization.

source.place: Proof (3): vanishing on the closed complement.

proof.text: Exactness of $i^*,c^*$ from [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] makes the cohomology of the cone of $\iota_A$ restrict to zero on both pieces. Each cohomology sheaf is zero by [lem-exc-open-closed-detection]; hence $\iota_A$ is invertible for $A\in\Dctf$. Apply [det-sf-comp-coherence-single] to $(\mathrm{id},p)$, $(i,\mathrm{id})$ and $(j',r)$: $F,G$ are exact and preserve sums on the localizing closures. Step 3 and [det-sf-determination-localizing] extend invertibility to every $A\in\Loc(\Dctf)$.

source.place: Proof (3): detection and localizing propagation using existing lemmas.

proof_origin.place: Proof (1)–(3), retaining the reviewed route and extracting the derived restriction and boundary-support arguments.

The re-split note is answered: the proof went from 6753 to 2203 characters in 5 steps. The old steps 2-4 became lem-sfb-derived-open-square-restriction: open restriction commutes with Rr_* on unbounded categories for all admissible Λ, via a Hom chain made of D(i_!)⊣D(i*), r*⊣Rr_*, the open base change from open-closed (4), D(j_!)⊣D(j*) and p*⊣Rp_*. It is true, with no properness needed, and checked on small cases (r=id, i=id, W empty). The old step 6 became lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero: c*Rr_*j_!A=0 for A in Dctf. It is true: j_!A is in Dctf by det-proper-image-localizing-open; proper base change uses the finite version (2) on Dctf, and the integral (3) and rational (3) versions on Dbc, since Dctf is contained in Dbc; and r^{-1}(Z) misses U. The item's statement and lean records are byte-identical to live, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Step 2's λ_A=(Rp_*η_{j'})^{-1}ρ type-checks. Step 3 is elementary adjunction calculus, with shift compatibility taken from node 1. Step 4 gets c*i_!=0 from open-closed (4). Step 5 uses exactness of the module pullbacks, open-closed detection (i is quasi-compact), coherence-single on (id,p), (i,id) and (j',r), and determination-localizing. Neither new node restates a parent clause, I found no cycle and no SGA citation, and the item is not in the dropped list.
